findings.issue_text: P0: Removal of per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource user search allows callers with only QUERY_USERS to receive the full unrestricted user list, a potential authorization bypass leaking all users in the realm

P1: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId() (authorization resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() (the group ID) to the granted set, so the UserModel.GROUPS filter matches nothing and group-scoped user visibility silently breaks

P1: Inside GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), hasPermission looks up resources by the resource UUID instead of the group ID, so per-group permissions are ignored and results are determined solely by whether an all-groups permission exists (all-or-nothing instead of per-group)
P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when only VIEW permission exists (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), allowing view-only admins to create/delete groups via requireManage()

P2: Group hierarchy is no longer honored when deriving visible users from group permissions — the new flat group-ID set filter means permissions on a parent group no longer surface users who are members only of subgroups, a regression from the documented group-chain semantics

P2: UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership semantic loosening — now grants map-roles/manage-membership to anyone with plain MANAGE on the user or MANAGE_MEMBERS on any group in the user's chain, a silent privilege widening relative to prior behavior

P3: GroupPermissions V1 canManage()/canView() changed from delegating to users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault() to hasOneAdminRole checks, dropping fine-grained user-permission grants and potentially changing behavior for V1 realm admins

P1: Per-user authorization filter removed from user search; callers with only query-users permission can now enumerate all users because getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty set when no group-scoped permissions exist and the session attribute is never set
P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage when caller has only view permission on all-groups, due to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) accepting either scope
P2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() no longer treats manage-users as unrestricted, changing empty-set semantics so manage-only admins may get inconsistent counts or unfiltered search results

getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs unbounded per-group permission evaluation (N+1: resource loads, policy loads, and full authz evaluations per group) on every admin user search/list/count call, with no pagination or batching

Per-element permission evaluation inside stream filters in GroupsResource.java:112 and GroupResource.java:177 runs a full authz evaluation per group, including a wasted negative resourceStore.findByName lookup and repeated policyStore.findByResource on the type resource, with no request-level memoization

Filter-after-pagination in GroupsResource.java:100–113 and GroupResource.java:176–178 applies canView filtering after the DB-level first/max window, causing pages to return fewer than max (or empty) results despite more viewable groups existing, and fetching rows only to discard them (wasted I/O and unpredictable effective page size)

P1: Removal of usersEvaluator::canView filter in UsersResource user search causes callers with per-user VIEW permissions but no group view permission to lose visibility of those users — response content drift

P1: GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() guard changed from canView() || canManage() to canView() only; a MANAGE_USERS-only admin with empty granted set gets unfiltered search results, gaining read visibility of every user

P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() passes hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so view-only callers satisfy canManage()/requireManage(), over-granting group create/update/delete at the admin API boundary; inconsistent with per-group canManage(GroupModel) which checks only MANAGE

P2: Public interface GroupPermissionEvaluator changed — getGroupsWithViewPermission() removed/renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and the getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) overload deleted, breaking external implementers/callers at compile time and changing semantics (group objects vs IDs, dropped canManage short-circuit)
P2: Public static helper ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes deleted without deprecation cycle or replacement shim, breaking external callers at compile time

P2: canViewMembers semantics broadened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS scope, and requireViewMembers switched from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers, changing prior distinct behavior; in V2 canViewMembers short-circuits on root.users().canView(), letting any user-viewer view members of all groups

P3: AdminPermissions.registerListener moved the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check from per-event to registration time, so feature state changes after startup would alter event handling and cleanup behavior for removed roles/groups/clients

P1: Per-user authorization filter (usersEvaluator::canView) removed from user search in UsersResource.java and BruteForceUsersResource.java, causing unauthorized data exposure when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns empty set (e.g., !root.isAdminSameRealm() or null realm resource server, or callers with only QUERY_USERS/QUERY_GROUPS) — searchForUserStream then runs unfiltered and returns all users to callers who cannot view them

P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on all groups to callers with only view permission (accepts either VIEW or MANAGE scope), allowing view-only group admins to pass requireManage() and create/modify group structure — privilege escalation

P2: requireViewMembers in GroupPermissions.java narrowed for manage-only admins — old getGroupsWithViewPermission allowed canView() || canManage(), new code delegates to canViewMembers, potentially denying member viewing to callers with manage-users but not view-users (functional regression for V1 deployments)

P2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in GroupPermissions.java drops the canManage() shortcut (previously returned empty set for canView() || canManage()), causing unexpected result narrowing for callers whose canView() is granted only via fine-grained user permissions, with possible behavioral drift between getUsersCount and search endpoints

P2: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission evaluates only the specific group resource and ignores all-groups grants when a specific resource exists, potentially denying callers with an all-groups manage permission operations on individual groups, contradicting testManageAllGroups expectations

P1: Security-relevant removal of per-user filter (usersEvaluator::canView) in UsersResource.searchForUser with no dedicated test coverage; reliance on session attribute honored by all storage providers
P1: Identical removal of per-user filtering in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser with zero test coverage for the brute-force search endpoint
P1: UserPermissionsV2 silently drops AdminRoles.ADMIN role from canView/canManage decisions with no replacement or test coverage
P2: getUsersCount restricted path using getGroupIdsWithViewPermission has no test for group-scoped permissions, leaving count/search consistency unverified
P2: requireViewMembers behavior change denying cross-realm admins and adding MANAGE_MEMBERS-grants-viewMembers path is untested

P2: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback-to-all-groups path only tested for happy case; missing negative tests for group-specific resource bypass and view-only permission not granting manage (canManage checks VIEW || MANAGE)
P3: Test exception assertions use broad catch (Exception) and may mask genuine server errors like NPEs
P3: AdminPermissions.registerListener refactor moves feature check to registration time with no test covering feature flag state changes

P1: Users restricted-group filtering can silently degrade to 'no restriction' — removal of .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) plus empty-set handling in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() can leak all users unfiltered (UsersResource.java:445-451, BruteForceUsersResource.java:144-151)
P1: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() checks root.users().canView() instead of groups().canView(), so V2 admins with only group-level view/manage grants get an empty set and unrestricted user listing

P1: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization-resource IDs instead of group IDs; should use groupResource.getName() which holds the group id (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~135-150)

P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts VIEW scope as sufficient for manage (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), letting view-only admins manage groups; likely copy/paste error (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~55-61)
P2: Empty-set is overloaded to mean both 'unrestricted' and 'no access' in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission contract; an Optional<Set<String>> or explicit unrestricted signal would remove ambiguity

P2: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from 10 inherited GroupPermissionManager interface methods (LSP violation), causing runtime failures if reached (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~170-211)

P2: Duplicated permission-evaluation logic between GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission and UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (and V1 MgmtPermissions variants); should be extracted into a shared helper to prevent drift

P3: Fields root, resourceStore, policyStore in GroupPermissions.java:56-58 widened from private final to protected final solely to support subclassing; composition or shared-helper approach would be better

UsersResource.searchForUser: per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) removed; group-attribute shortcut only set when groupIds is non-empty, so user-level fine-grained view permission callers get unrestricted searchForUserStream results (P1)
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope via hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), granting manage rights (group creation/deletion) to view-only admins (P1)

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to the all-groups resource for any unknown group id, including non-existent ones, without verifying group existence or constraining lookup to the Groups type (P2)

GroupResource.getSubGroups: global-view fast path (canViewGlobal || canView(g)) removed; every subgroup now filtered individually, silently truncating group trees for callers with parent-group view but no child resource/policy (P2)

AdminPermissions.registerListener: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved to registration time only; runtime feature enablement would leave events dropped and cleanup-on-delete listeners unregistered (P3)

GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission uses resourceStore.findByName across the resource server, not scoped to the Groups type, so a non-group resource with a matching name could be evaluated for group permission decisions, risking NPE or mis-evaluation (P3)

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when only VIEW permission exists (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), allowing view-only admins to create/delete groups via requireManage()

This is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment (canManage should require MANAGE only, while canView can accept VIEW or MANAGE).

per_golden_matches.golden_comment: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
per_golden_matches.matched_candidate: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId() (authorization resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() (the group ID) to the granted set, so the UserModel.GROUPS filter matches nothing and group-scoped user visibility silently breaks
per_golden_matches.reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same core bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is returning/using the authorization resource UUID (groupResource.getId()) instead of the actual group identifier (resource name) that downstream code (UserModel.GROUPS filters, user counts) expects. This mismatch causes group-scoped VIEW/MANAGE permissions to not translate into correct group IDs for filtering and may effectively degrade to type-level checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P0: Removal of per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) in UsersResource user search allows callers with only QUERY_USERS to receive the full unrestricted user list, a potential authorization bypass leaking all users in the realm

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the per-user authorization gate `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` directly to `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` *only if* `groupIds` is non-empty. For callers who cannot `canView()` users and also have no group view-member permissions (so `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set), no session attribute is set and there is no longer any per-user filtering in this method, so the search stream can become unrestricted relative to the caller’s permissions. Given `UserPermissions.canQuery()` allows `QUERY_USERS` without `canView()`, this creates a plausible authorization bypass/leak introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() adds groupResource.getId() (authorization resource UUID) instead of groupResource.getName() (the group ID) to the granted set, so the UserModel.GROUPS filter matches nothing and group-scoped user visibility silently breaks
matched_golden_ids: In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. Both describe the same core bug: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is returning/using the authorization resource UUID (groupResource.getId()) instead of the actual group identifier (resource name) that downstream code (UserModel.GROUPS filters, user counts) expects. This mismatch causes group-scoped VIEW/MANAGE permissions to not translate into correct group IDs for filtering and may effectively degrade to type-level checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Inside GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), hasPermission looks up resources by the resource UUID instead of the group ID, so per-group permissions are ignored and results are determined solely by whether an all-groups permission exists (all-or-nothing instead of per-group)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, the callback iterates `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and passes `groupResource.getId()` into `hasPermission(...)`, then adds `groupResource.getId()` to the granted set. However, `hasPermission(String groupId, ...)` treats its argument as a *group id/name* and does `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)`. Passing the authorization resource UUID (`Resource.getId()`) will typically not match the resource name (which, per `AdminPermissionsSchema.resolveGroup`, is based on `group.getId()`). As a result `resource` becomes null and `hasPermission` falls back to evaluating the generic `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (“all-groups”) resource, making the result effectively all-or-nothing rather than per-group, and returning resource UUIDs rather than group IDs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when only VIEW permission exists (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), allowing view-only admins to create/delete groups via requireManage()
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() uses a fallback permission check that includes VIEW and MANAGE, causing users with only VIEW permission to pass canManage() and gain write/manage capabilities. This is the same underlying issue described in the golden comment (canManage should require MANAGE only, while canView can accept VIEW or MANAGE).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Group hierarchy is no longer honored when deriving visible users from group permissions — the new flat group-ID set filter means permissions on a parent group no longer surface users who are members only of subgroups, a regression from the documented group-chain semantics

P2: UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles/canManageGroupMembership semantic loosening — now grants map-roles/manage-membership to anyone with plain MANAGE on the user or MANAGE_MEMBERS on any group in the user's chain, a silent privilege widening relative to prior behavior

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles` and `canManageGroupMembership`, but the alleged privilege widening is not supported. Previously, both methods granted access when `canManage(user)` was true. In `UserPermissionsV2`, `canManage(user)` already returned true for either a direct `MANAGE` permission on the user or via `canManageByGroup(user)` (group-chain `MANAGE_MEMBERS`). Therefore, the new logic (`hasPermission(..., MANAGE, <specific-scope>) || canManageByGroup(user)`) does not newly grant these capabilities compared to prior behavior; it largely preserves the same effective conditions while changing the admin-role shortcut check.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: GroupPermissions V1 canManage()/canView() changed from delegating to users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault() to hasOneAdminRole checks, dropping fine-grained user-permission grants and potentially changing behavior for V1 realm admins

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissions (V1), canManage() changed from `root.users().canManageDefault()` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)` and canView() changed from `root.users().canViewDefault()` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`. But in this same diff, `UserPermissions.canManageDefault()` and `UserPermissions.canViewDefault()` are removed and (as shown) they were simply wrappers around those same `hasOneAdminRole(...)` checks, not fine-grained permission evaluations. So the change does not verifiably drop fine-grained grants or change behavior for V1 based on what’s in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Per-user authorization filter removed from user search; callers with only query-users permission can now enumerate all users because getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns empty set when no group-scoped permissions exist and the session attribute is never set

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser (and BruteForceUsersResource), the explicit per-user permission filter was removed: previously `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`; now it passes the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)` with no filter. The only remaining restriction is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. If that set is empty, no session attribute is set, so the search is not constrained by group IDs at all in this method. Given `UserPermissions.canQuery()` allows `QUERY_USERS` without `canView()`, this diff can enable a caller who can query but lacks view permissions (and has no group-scoped view-members permissions, hence empty groupIds) to receive search results they shouldn’t.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants global manage when caller has only view permission on all-groups, due to hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) accepting either scope

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2` class, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` when the caller lacks `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` (see `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`). The helper `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* of the provided scopes is granted. This means a caller with only global group `VIEW` permission (all-groups) would be treated as having global manage permission, which is an authorization escalation and inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` (which requires `MANAGE` only).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() no longer treats manage-users as unrestricted, changing empty-set semantics so manage-only admins may get inconsistent counts or unfiltered search results

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` to return an empty set when `root.users().canView()` is true (instead of `canView() || canManage()`). But in `UserPermissions.canView()` (see updated logic in `UserPermissions`), having the manage-users role (`AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS`) already implies `canView()` is true (`root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`), so “manage-users is no longer unrestricted” is not supported by the diff. In the call sites (`UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource`), group restriction is only applied when the returned set is non-empty, which will not occur for manage-users admins given `canView()` is true.

adjudication_records.issue_text: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() performs unbounded per-group permission evaluation (N+1: resource loads, policy loads, and full authz evaluations per group) on every admin user search/list/count call, with no pagination or batching

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces/expands a code path where user listing/counting can trigger per-group authorization evaluation over *all* group resources. In `GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, it iterates `resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and for each group resource calls `hasPermission(...)`, which performs `policyStore.findByResource(...)` (in some paths) and a full `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))`. There is no pagination/batching or limiting; it potentially evaluates permissions once per group resource. This set is then used from user endpoints for restricted admins, e.g. `UsersResource#getUsersCount(...): session.users().getUsersCount(..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())` and `UsersResource#searchForUser(...)` now calls `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (unconditionally, though it may early-return empty for global viewers). This is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern (N-per-group evaluations), not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Per-element permission evaluation inside stream filters in GroupsResource.java:112 and GroupResource.java:177 runs a full authz evaluation per group, including a wasted negative resourceStore.findByName lookup and repeated policyStore.findByResource on the type resource, with no request-level memoization

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes both GroupResource#getSubGroups and GroupsResource#getGroups to always call per-element permission checks via `.filter(auth.groups()::canView)` / `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)` instead of short-circuiting with a precomputed `canViewGlobal` boolean. In the new V2 implementation, `GroupPermissionsV2.canView(GroupModel)` calls `hasPermission(group.getId(), ...)`, which performs `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` and, when no per-group resource exists, falls back to the type resource and calls `policyStore.findByResource(server, resource)` before evaluating permissions. Because this is invoked inside the stream filter, these store lookups/evaluations can repeat for every group in the result stream, with no request-level memoization shown in the diff. This is a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Filter-after-pagination in GroupsResource.java:100–113 and GroupResource.java:176–178 applies canView filtering after the DB-level first/max window, causing pages to return fewer than max (or empty) results despite more viewable groups existing, and fetching rows only to discard them (wasted I/O and unpredictable effective page size)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsResource#getGroups` (around lines 100–113 in the diff), the group search methods (`searchGroupsByAttributes`, `searchForGroupByNameStream`, `getTopLevelGroupsStream`) are called with `firstResult/maxResults`, and only afterwards the result stream is filtered with `stream.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`. This means the DB-level window is applied before permission filtering, so a page can come back with fewer than `maxResults` (or empty) even if additional viewable groups exist beyond the fetched window, and rows may be fetched only to be discarded. However, the finding’s reference to `GroupResource#getSubGroups` is not accurate in the diff: it uses `-1, -1` (no DB pagination) and then paginates after filtering via `paginatedStream(...)`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Removal of usersEvaluator::canView filter in UsersResource user search causes callers with per-user VIEW permissions but no group view permission to lose visibility of those users — response content drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` in `UsersResource#searchForUser`, but that change would not inherently cause callers to *lose* visibility of users they can view per-user; if anything, removing a filter can only keep the same set or expand it. Also, the new group restriction setup (`getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` + `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`) is only applied when the returned set is non-empty; for a caller with per-user VIEW permission but no group-member view permissions, `groupIds` would plausibly be empty and no restriction would be applied at this layer. The finding’s claimed “loss of visibility” is not supported by the shown changes (the more plausible concern from this diff would be over-exposure if no later filtering occurs, but that is the opposite of the finding).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() guard changed from canView() || canManage() to canView() only; a MANAGE_USERS-only admin with empty granted set gets unfiltered search results, gaining read visibility of every user

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims a MANAGE_USERS-only admin could get unintended read visibility because getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() now short-circuits only on canView(). But in this diff, UserPermissions.canView() explicitly returns true for admins with MANAGE_USERS (and also for any MANAGE permission via authz), so a MANAGE_USERS-only admin already has global view and is expected to see all users. The alleged state “canManage() true while canView() false” is not supported by the permission logic shown here, so the described escalation is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() passes hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), so view-only callers satisfy canManage()/requireManage(), over-granting group create/update/delete at the admin API boundary; inconsistent with per-group canManage(GroupModel) which checks only MANAGE

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller with only the `VIEW` scope on the all-groups resource-type would satisfy `canManage()` (and thus `requireManage()` from the base `GroupPermissions`), potentially allowing manage-level operations guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` (e.g., group creation). This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel group)`, which checks only `MANAGE`, and matches the finding’s over-grant concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Public interface GroupPermissionEvaluator changed — getGroupsWithViewPermission() removed/renamed to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and the getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel) overload deleted, breaking external implementers/callers at compile time and changing semantics (group objects vs IDs, dropped canManage short-circuit)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a source-incompatible change to the public `GroupPermissionEvaluator` interface: `Set<String> getGroupsWithViewPermission()` is renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and the `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` method is removed entirely (see `GroupPermissionEvaluator` and corresponding implementation changes in `GroupPermissions`). This will break any external implementers/callers at compile time unless they update. The semantic shift from “groups” to “group IDs” is also explicit in the new method name and Javadoc. However, within this diff, all in-repo call sites are updated and the change appears intentional (new V2 permissions), so it’s an API compatibility concern rather than a verifiable functional defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Public static helper ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes deleted without deprecation cycle or replacement shim, breaking external callers at compile time

adjudication.rationale: The diff does delete the public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` from `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java` with no deprecated forwarding shim left in place. Call sites in-tree are updated (e.g., `GroupsResource` now calls `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)` directly), but any out-of-tree code that compiled against this public helper will now fail to compile. Whether this requires a deprecation cycle is a compatibility/process concern rather than a runtime correctness defect evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: canViewMembers semantics broadened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS scope, and requireViewMembers switched from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers, changing prior distinct behavior; in V2 canViewMembers short-circuits on root.users().canView(), letting any user-viewer view members of all groups

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupPermissions.canViewMembers(GroupModel)` to treat `MANAGE_MEMBERS` as sufficient (`hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`), and `requireViewMembers` now delegates to `canViewMembers`. However, the removed method `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel group)` (previously used by `requireViewMembers`) already granted access when `hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)` and also short-circuited for global user view/manage (`root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()`). So `requireViewMembers` behavior is not meaningfully broadened by this change, and the claim that this introduces a new “any user-viewer can view members of all groups” behavior in V2 is not supported by the diff because the pre-change path already allowed global user-viewers as well.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: AdminPermissions.registerListener moved the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) check from per-event to registration time, so feature state changes after startup would alter event handling and cleanup behavior for removed roles/groups/clients

adjudication.rationale: The diff in AdminPermissions.registerListener does move the Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ) guard from inside onEvent(...) to wrapping the manager.register(...) call. Previously the listener was always registered but was a no-op when the feature was disabled; now it is not registered at all unless the feature is enabled at registration time. This does change behavior if the feature flag could change after startup/registration (events would start/stop being handled differently), though the diff alone doesn’t prove that runtime toggling is expected/supported.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Per-user authorization filter (usersEvaluator::canView) removed from user search in UsersResource.java and BruteForceUsersResource.java, causing unauthorized data exposure when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns empty set (e.g., !root.isAdminSameRealm() or null realm resource server, or callers with only QUERY_USERS/QUERY_GROUPS) — searchForUserStream then runs unfiltered and returns all users to callers who cannot view them

adjudication.rationale: In both UsersResource.searchForUser(...) and BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...), the explicit per-user authorization filter was removed: `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` became a direct call to `searchForUserStream(...)` passed into `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining narrowing is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. If that set is empty for a caller who still reaches these endpoints (e.g., due to realm/resource-server constraints inside permission evaluators), the code no longer applies `usersEvaluator::canView` at all, so the returned stream is no longer verifiably constrained by per-user authorization in this method. This is a concrete security/correctness regression relative to the previous behavior shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on all groups to callers with only view permission (accepts either VIEW or MANAGE scope), allowing view-only group admins to pass requireManage() and create/modify group structure — privilege escalation

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller granted only the `VIEW` scope on the groups *resource type* (the fallback “all-groups” resource when `groupId == null`) will satisfy `canManage()`. Since `requireManage()` in `GroupPermissions` is based on `canManage()`, this effectively treats VIEW as sufficient for “manage” checks at the non-group-specific level (e.g., operations guarded by `requireManage()` rather than `requireManage(group)`), which is a privilege escalation relative to the method’s intent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: requireViewMembers in GroupPermissions.java narrowed for manage-only admins — old getGroupsWithViewPermission allowed canView() || canManage(), new code delegates to canViewMembers, potentially denying member viewing to callers with manage-users but not view-users (functional regression for V1 deployments)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupPermissions.requireViewMembers` to check `canViewMembers(group)` instead of the removed `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)`. But `canViewMembers` still grants access for manage-users admins because it short-circuits with `if (root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()) return true;`. In `UserPermissions.canView()`, having `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` is sufficient (`root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`), so a caller with MANAGE_USERS (even without VIEW_USERS) will still satisfy `root.users().canView()` and not be denied. Therefore the claimed regression for “manage-only admins” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission in GroupPermissions.java drops the canManage() shortcut (previously returned empty set for canView() || canManage()), causing unexpected result narrowing for callers whose canView() is granted only via fine-grained user permissions, with possible behavioral drift between getUsersCount and search endpoints

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupPermissions.getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and the early-return condition from `root.users().canView() || root.users().canManage()` to only `root.users().canView()` (services/.../GroupPermissions.java). However, in the shown code `root.users().canView()` already covers manage-capable admins: `UserPermissions.canView()` returns true for `AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS` and for user permissions granting `MANAGE` (it checks `VIEW` or `MANAGE`). Therefore a caller who can manage users would also satisfy `canView()`, so dropping the explicit `canManage()` shortcut does not verifiably narrow results based on this diff. The claimed behavioral drift with fine-grained user permissions is not demonstrated by the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission evaluates only the specific group resource and ignores all-groups grants when a specific resource exists, potentially denying callers with an all-groups manage permission operations on individual groups, contradicting testManageAllGroups expectations

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`, when a specific group resource exists (`resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns non-null), the method evaluates permissions only against that specific `ResourcePermission(resource, ...)` and never checks the resource-type ("all-groups") resource (`getResourceTypeResource(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE)`). The fallback to the resource-type resource is only performed when the specific resource is null. This means a caller with an all-groups scope permission (e.g., MANAGE on `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`) can be denied on an individual group if that group has a dedicated resource, which matches the finding and can contradict the intended/mentioned fallback semantics in `testManageAllGroups` comments.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Security-relevant removal of per-user filter (usersEvaluator::canView) in UsersResource.searchForUser with no dedicated test coverage; reliance on session attribute honored by all storage providers

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove an explicit per-user permission filter in `UsersResource.searchForUser`: `session.users().searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` becomes an unfiltered stream passed to `toRepresentation(...)`. At the same time, access restriction is shifted toward setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` (now always set when non-empty) and relying on providers honoring this session attribute during `searchForUserStream`. From the diff alone, it’s not verifiable that `toRepresentation(...)` still enforces `usersEvaluator.canView` (its body isn’t shown), so the claim of an actual security defect can’t be proven. However, the change is clearly security-sensitive and creates a concrete concern: correctness/security now depends on all user storage providers respecting that session attribute, and there is no diff-visible targeted test ensuring providers that don’t honor it won’t leak results.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Identical removal of per-user filtering in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser with zero test coverage for the brute-force search endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser/searchForUserStream, the diff does not remove any per-user permission filter: previously it simply did `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and passed the stream to `toRepresentation(...)` (no `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` existed there). The change only inlines the stream creation and changes the session attribute from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` without the surrounding `if (!auth.users().canView())` block. Also, the claim of “zero test coverage for the brute-force search endpoint” cannot be verified from this diff alone (the diff adds tests, but doesn’t prove absence of existing brute-force tests).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: UserPermissionsV2 silently drops AdminRoles.ADMIN role from canView/canManage decisions with no replacement or test coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the short-circuit checks in `UserPermissionsV2`: `canView` changes from `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)` to only `MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS`, and `canManage` drops `AdminRoles.ADMIN` as well. Nothing in this diff shows an explicit replacement guaranteeing equivalent behavior for callers who only have `AdminRoles.ADMIN`, and the newly added tests (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, plus edits elsewhere) do not cover the `AdminRoles.ADMIN` case. Whether this is an actual regression depends on external semantics (e.g., whether `ADMIN` is composite of `MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS`), which is not verifiable from the diff alone, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded permission-model change that merits review/justification/tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: getUsersCount restricted path using getGroupIdsWithViewPermission has no test for group-scoped permissions, leaving count/search consistency unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes restricted counting paths in `UsersResource.getUsersCount(...)` from `auth.groups().getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` in multiple branches (e.g., lines around `getUsersCount(realm, ..., auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission())`). While new tests were added for group-scoped permissions affecting *user search visibility* (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` asserts results of `users().search(...)` after granting `VIEW_MEMBERS`/`MANAGE_MEMBERS`), the diff shows no test that exercises the corresponding *count* endpoint under the same group-scoped permissions to verify count/search consistency after this behavioral change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: requireViewMembers behavior change denying cross-realm admins and adding MANAGE_MEMBERS-grants-viewMembers path is untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `requireViewMembers` to call `canViewMembers(group)` (GroupPermissions.java), but `canViewMembers` is also updated to accept both `VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE` and `MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE` (line change: `hasPermission(..., VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE)`), which matches the previous behavior of `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` that `requireViewMembers` used before (it already treated MANAGE_MEMBERS as sufficient). Also, both the old and new paths include the same-realm restriction (`!root.isAdminSameRealm()` returns false/empty), so “denying cross-realm admins” is not a verifiable behavior change from this diff alone. Finally, the added test `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` explicitly exercises the MANAGE_MEMBERS => can view user path (`testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers`) and the VIEW_MEMBERS case (`testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers`), so the claim that this path is untested is contradicted by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission fallback-to-all-groups path only tested for happy case; missing negative tests for group-specific resource bypass and view-only permission not granting manage (canManage checks VIEW || MANAGE)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial new authorization behavior in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission()` including a fallback to the resource-type (“all-groups”) resource when a group resource is not found (or has no policies) and also changes `canManage()` to return true when either `VIEW` or `MANAGE` scope is granted (`canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`). The new tests (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) exercise mostly happy paths (e.g., manage-all-groups works), but do not add negative assertions around these new semantics (e.g., that a VIEW-only all-groups permission does not allow manage operations, if that is intended, and edge cases around group-specific resource vs fallback). This is a concrete test-coverage gap tied to the new logic, but the diff alone does not prove the behavior is incorrect because the interface Javadoc for V2 explicitly mentions VIEW-or-MANAGE for `canManage()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Test exception assertions use broad catch (Exception) and may mask genuine server errors like NPEs

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/keeps several test blocks that catch a broad `Exception` and then assert its type, e.g. in `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` multiple places: `catch (Exception ex) { assertThat(ex, instanceOf(ForbiddenException.class)); }` and similarly for `NotFoundException`. This can indeed mask unexpected failures (e.g., client-side runtime exceptions or other errors) by treating them as part of the expected path until the type assertion runs, making diagnosis harder and potentially hiding real regressions compared to catching the specific expected exception type.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: AdminPermissions.registerListener refactor moves feature check to registration time with no test covering feature flag state changes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change behavior in `AdminPermissions.registerListener`: the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check was moved from inside `onEvent(...)` to wrap the `manager.register(...)` call. Previously, the listener was always registered and would start/stop acting based on the feature flag at event time; now it only exists if the flag is enabled at registration time. Whether runtime feature-flag changes are supported isn’t shown in the diff, and the claim about “no test covering feature flag state changes” can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the behavioral shift/edge-case is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Users restricted-group filtering can silently degrade to 'no restriction' — removal of .filter(usersEvaluator::canView) plus empty-set handling in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() can leak all users unfiltered (UsersResource.java:445-451, BruteForceUsersResource.java:144-151)

adjudication.rationale: In UsersResource.searchForUser(), the diff removes the explicit per-user permission filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now always calls `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` without any subsequent filtering in this method. At the same time, the only narrowing mechanism shown here is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` *only if* `groupIds` is non-empty. If `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set for a non-global viewer (e.g., caller lacks global view and has no group-member view grants), no session attribute is set and the query is executed unrestricted by this code path—where previously the `usersEvaluator::canView` filter would still prevent over-disclosure. The same pattern is introduced in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(). This is a plausible security/correctness regression grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() checks root.users().canView() instead of groups().canView(), so V2 admins with only group-level view/manage grants get an empty set and unrestricted user listing

adjudication.rationale: In both GroupPermissions#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() and the new GroupPermissionsV2#getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), the early-return condition is `if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();`. That only yields an empty set when the caller can already view users globally (so no group restriction is needed). For an admin with only group-level grants (e.g., VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS) and no global user-view capability, `root.users().canView()` would be false and the method proceeds to compute and return the granted group IDs by checking `hasPermission(..., VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS)`. The finding’s claim that group-level-only admins get an empty set and thus an unrestricted user listing is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns authorization-resource IDs instead of group IDs; should use groupResource.getName() which holds the group id (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~135-150)

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), it iterates authz Resources and passes groupResource.getId() into hasPermission(...), and also adds groupResource.getId() to the returned set. But hasPermission(String groupId, ...) treats its parameter as a *resource name* by calling resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId). Resource.getId() is the internal authz resource identifier, while the group id is stored as the Resource name (see AdminPermissionsSchema: resolveGroup returns group.getId(), and getOrCreateResource looks up by findByName(resourceServer, id)). Therefore this method will both (a) evaluate permissions against the wrong resource (likely falling back to the all-groups resource) and (b) return authz resource IDs instead of group IDs; it should use groupResource.getName().

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts VIEW scope as sufficient for manage (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), letting view-only admins manage groups; likely copy/paste error (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~55-61)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2` class, `canManage()` (no specific group) returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller granted only the `VIEW` scope on the all-groups resource type would satisfy `canManage()`. Any endpoints guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` (which delegates to `canManage()`) could then allow management operations to view-only principals. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` which correctly requires `MANAGE` only, and strongly suggests an authorization/copy-paste mistake.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Empty-set is overloaded to mean both 'unrestricted' and 'no access' in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission contract; an Optional<Set<String>> or explicit unrestricted signal would remove ambiguity

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returning `Collections.emptySet()` both when access is unrestricted (interface Javadoc: “If UserPermissionEvaluator#canView() evaluates to true, returns empty set.”; implementations: `if (root.users().canView()) return Collections.emptySet();`) and when there is effectively no usable group-based access (e.g., `!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, `server == null`, or no granted permissions in `GroupPermissionsV2` all return empty). Call sites in `UsersResource`/`BruteForceUsersResource` only set `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` when the set is non-empty, so an empty set is implicitly treated as “no restriction”. This makes the empty-set meaning ambiguous in the API/contract, even if the overall behavior might still be correct depending on downstream logic not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: GroupPermissionsV2 throws UnsupportedOperationException from 10 inherited GroupPermissionManager interface methods (LSP violation), causing runtime failures if reached (GroupPermissionsV2.java:~170-211)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the new `GroupPermissionsV2` (which extends `GroupPermissions`, and thus still fulfills the same management-capable type) overrides multiple inherited management operations to throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions` in `GroupPermissionsV2.java:~170-211`). Since `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns this implementation, any existing code path that expects `root.groups()` to support the management API could now fail at runtime if it calls one of these methods. The diff alone doesn’t prove these methods are reachable in normal V2 execution, but it is a concrete, change-introduced compatibility/architecture risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Duplicated permission-evaluation logic between GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission and UserPermissionsV2.hasPermission (and V1 MgmtPermissions variants); should be extracted into a shared helper to prevent drift

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new private permission-evaluation helper in `GroupPermissionsV2` (`private boolean hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`) that performs generic resource/scope evaluation with an “all-groups” fallback via `AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`. `UserPermissionsV2` already contains its own `hasPermission(...)` helper (signature shown in the diff) used for analogous scope checks. This indicates parallel, potentially overlapping implementations of the same evaluation pattern across V2 permission evaluators, creating a maintainability/drift risk (architecture concern), though it is not a directly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Fields root, resourceStore, policyStore in GroupPermissions.java:56-58 widened from private final to protected final solely to support subclassing; composition or shared-helper approach would be better

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes `GroupPermissions` fields `root`, `resourceStore`, and `policyStore` from `private final` to `protected final` (services/.../GroupPermissions.java) and introduces `GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions` which directly uses those members (e.g., `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)`, `resourceStore.findByType(...)`, `policyStore.findByResource(...)`). This is an API/encapsulation design concern (visibility widened to enable subclass access) rather than a functional defect, and a reviewer could reasonably suggest alternatives like delegation/composition or helper methods to avoid exposing internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: UsersResource.searchForUser: per-user authorization filter (.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)) removed; group-attribute shortcut only set when groupIds is non-empty, so user-level fine-grained view permission callers get unrestricted searchForUserStream results (P1)
GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope via hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), granting manage rights (group creation/deletion) to view-only admins (P1)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller with only the `VIEW` scope on the (all-)groups resource will satisfy `canManage()` and thus `requireManage()` checks that gate “manage” operations. This is a verifiable permission escalation in the diff: `VIEW` is treated as sufficient for “manage” at the global level (`groupId == null`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() falls back to the all-groups resource for any unknown group id, including non-existent ones, without verifying group existence or constraining lookup to the Groups type (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(String groupId, String... scopes)`, the lookup is `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (no type constraint). If that returns null for any input (including a non-existent/unknown group id), the method falls back to evaluating permissions against the global resource-type resource for `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`) as long as there is at least one policy for it. That means an arbitrary/unknown `groupId` can still be authorized based solely on the presence of an all-groups policy, without verifying the group exists or that the found resource (if any) is actually a Groups resource.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupResource.getSubGroups: global-view fast path (canViewGlobal || canView(g)) removed; every subgroup now filtered individually, silently truncating group trees for callers with parent-group view but no child resource/policy (P2)

adjudication.rationale: In GroupResource.getSubGroups the old filter was `canViewGlobal || auth.groups().canView(g)` where `canViewGlobal` was `auth.groups().canView()` (i.e., global view), not “can view the parent group”. If the caller only has view on the parent but not children, they were already filtered individually before this change (because `canViewGlobal` would be false). The diff only removes the optimization when `canViewGlobal` is true, but in the permission evaluators shown (notably GroupPermissionsV2), global view via roles or “all-groups” permission implies `canView(g)` will also return true (it falls back to the all-groups resource-type permission when a per-group resource is missing). So the claim about truncating trees for parent-only viewers is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AdminPermissions.registerListener: ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ feature check moved to registration time only; runtime feature enablement would leave events dropped and cleanup-on-delete listeners unregistered (P3)

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly moves the `Profile.isFeatureEnabled(Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ)` check from inside `onEvent(...)` to wrapping the `manager.register(...)` call in `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (so no listener is registered at all when the feature is disabled at registration time). The finding’s consequence (events/cleanup won’t run if the feature becomes enabled later) is a valid concern *if* feature flags can change after registration, but that runtime-enable assumption is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission uses resourceStore.findByName across the resource server, not scoped to the Groups type, so a non-group resource with a matching name could be evaluated for group permission decisions, risking NPE or mis-evaluation (P3)

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the per-group resource is resolved via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (where `groupId` is used as the resource name). The diff does not show any check that the returned `Resource` is of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`, so if `findByName` is not type-scoped and names are not guaranteed unique across all resource types in the same server, the permission evaluation could be performed against a non-group resource. The diff alone does not confirm whether the underlying store enforces unique names or type scoping, so this is a concrete hardening/correctness concern rather than a definitively provable defect from the patch itself.
